solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Banter is not good at home over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing over another sits above it, so the earlier part is written first

blocks.note: the opposite of good
someone at home is in
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the chit-chat at home has gone sour over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: BAD and IN come first, stacked over AGE in this down clue, giving BADINAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful teasing conversation, a close synonym for light-hearted joking exchanges.

blocks.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
a tattoo is ink, and to ink someone is to tattoo them

explanation.surface: A monarch's odd habit of getting tattooed.
explanation.walkthrough: K for king is followed by INK, the slang word for a tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A kink is an odd twist in someone's character, a peculiar habit or eccentricity.

blocks.note: what is popular is in fashion
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A well-liked nurse who is nonetheless stingy or unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective describing the nurse, but it is the verb, as in 'I mean to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to have it in mind as a purpose, which is the verb sense of mean.

indicators.note: when something is out it has been removed, so one letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a faculty is a division of a university
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A flawed university department has been found out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take FACULTY and remove the C for caught, a cricket scoring convention, to leave FAULTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something faulty has defects, so it is flawed and not perfect.

clue.text: To draw attention to tirade is outrageous

blocks.note: to flag something is to point it out
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: Someone says that highlighting a furious outburst is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To draw attention to' is the wordplay for the first piece, not the definition; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant offence is glaring and shocking, openly scandalous in the way outrageous behaviour is.

indicators.note: going back the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force
too means also, as well

explanation.surface: An instruction to gauge a force that also comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: F is followed by TOO turned round, giving FOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot is an imperial unit of length, twelve inches, used for measuring distances.

clue.text: Engineer can hide a country house in Spain

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A builder could conceal a rural Spanish mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun doing the hiding, but it is an imperative telling you to rearrange the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or its main residence in Spain or Latin America.

indicators.note: something returned goes back where it came from, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a kitty is a shared pool of money

explanation.surface: A phone call: the cat came home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' suggests a cat, but here it is a shared fund of money, and 'Ring' suggests a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a circular shape formed by a curve closing on itself, much like a ring.

blocks.note: to select is to pick
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Choose the French condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' could be a verb meaning enjoy; here it is the noun for a tangy condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickle is a chunky preserved condiment served with food, one kind of relish.

blocks.note: first meaning: a device giving illumination
second meaning: not heavy

explanation.surface: A lamp that is easy to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of a portable lamp; the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a source of illumination and an adjective meaning of little weight.

indicators.note: at regular intervals means taking every other letter along the word

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inserts trap' reads like an instruction to set a trap; the word is only the source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A net is a mesh used for catching fish or animals, a kind of snare.

blocks.note: to run something is to supervise it
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A police hierarchy: the ranking officer oversaw the detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' suggests a police grade; it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid food smells stale and sour, so it is offensive to the nose, as rank means.

clue.text: Failure as everyone gets upset in wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run bottom to top
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: everyone is all
a copse is a small wood

explanation.surface: Things fall apart when everybody gets agitated in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as everyone being distressed, but in a down clue it means turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a sudden breakdown, as when a business or plan fails completely.

clue.text: Regularly ahead of time by end of day

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter
arriving ahead of time is being early

explanation.surface: Someone who is always punctual, getting things done before the day is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' only joins the two pieces; the final letter of day goes first, then EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something yearly recurs once every year, at fixed intervals, so it happens on a regular basis.

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports something sits beneath it, so it is written second

blocks.note: the lark is a songbird
a spur is a side branch, as of a railway line

explanation.surface: A bird perched on a plant's branch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is; LARK sits above SPUR because the branch supports the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a flowering garden plant with tall spikes of blue or purple blooms, related to delphiniums.

indicators.note: turned around every which way, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An obsessive who likes to lounge about.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the contradiction: a fanatic is the last person to laze around.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is someone with extreme, uncompromising devotion to a cause, which is what a fanatic is.

blocks.note: first meaning: shove forcefully
second meaning: the main point

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as advice to press the main point; the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for shoving forward and a noun for the central point of a case.

blocks.note: first meaning: confine, especially in wartime
second meaning: a junior learning on the job

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like an order to hold back a junior; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine someone, often a foreign national in war; an intern is also a junior on work placement.

blocks.note: the setter refers to themselves as I, and setter's is read as setter is, so I'M
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Fetch the crossword compiler's glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the person who wrote the clue, so 'setter's' means I am, shortened to I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To import goods is to bring them into a country from abroad.

clue.text: Hear song of praise for that man

indicators.note: listening to a word catches only its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a hymn is a song of praise

explanation.surface: An invitation to listen to a song praising a particular man.
explanation.walkthrough: The N in the song's name is silent, so it is said the same as the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Him is the object pronoun used when pointing to a particular male person.

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
to air something is to show it off

explanation.surface: A piece of work shown off on a stone doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds, abbreviated st.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single tread in a flight of steps inside a building.

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the oak is a tree

explanation.surface: An instruction to water a little tree thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small, placed before the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something is to wet it through completely, just as drenching does.

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
to raise is to increase

explanation.surface: Discreetly win more support.
explanation.walkthrough: Piano, marked p in sheet music, is the musical direction to play softly.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is spoken admiration or commendation, an expression of approval for someone.

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and topless means it has gone

blocks.note: to haunt a place is to go there often

explanation.surface: A rude instruction to drop in often on a scantily clad family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the H from the top of HAUNT to leave AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, one kind of family member.

blocks.note: first meaning: move past
second meaning: a permit to enter

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'follow the rules of the licence'; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is to move past something; a pass is also a document granting permission to enter.

clue.text: Nervous as second tyrant initially telephoned

indicators.note: at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
the opening letter
rung up is British for telephoned

explanation.surface: Someone is jittery because a despot has just called.
explanation.walkthrough: To ring someone up is everyday British for phoning them, so rung up means telephoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strung up is tense and on edge, as though wound tight, which means anxious.
